mechanism_narrative: A continued rebound in WORKPLACES mobility raises weekday trip chains and lunch-time discretionary visits, so RETAIL_REC should be higher over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -51.7 to -20.6 over the last three weekly means
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES does not continue rising or RETAIL_REC remains flat-to-lower over the next 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility falls from elevated levels, people spend more time outside the home and shift demand into shopping and dining venues, lifting RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines below 8 points after a week above 10 points
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL moved from 13.1 at t-2w to 7.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL drops below the trigger but RETAIL_REC does not rise in the following week, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates commuting normalization; the combined effect increases retail visits during commutes and after work, so RETAIL_REC rises over two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -53.9 to -43.6 while WORKPLACES improved from -51.7 to -20.6
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise together but RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 14 days, the interaction claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PARKS mobility below prior positive readings signals a shift away from outdoor leisure and back toward indoor commercial activity, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below 0 after being positive the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS was 6.1 at t-2w and 7.4 at t-0w after -7.3 at t-1w
failure_condition: If PARKS remains positive while RETAIL_REC still rises, or PARKS falls below zero without any retail recovery over four weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently weak GROCERY_PHARM mobility together with lower RESIDENTIAL mobility implies fewer routine essential trips and more substitution toward discretionary shopping trips, which should raise RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved from 6.6 to -3.1 while RESIDENTIAL stayed above 7
failure_condition: If both GROCERY_PHARM stays weak and RESIDENTIAL stays elevated but RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT stays below -45 for multiple weeks, the city is still in a suppressed movement regime that limits retail foot traffic, so RETAIL_REC should remain lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -45 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -44.7, -53.9, -50.3, and -43.6 across the four observed weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT remains below -45 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A positive turn in PARKS combined with only a mild recovery in WORKPLACES reflects leisure-oriented movement rather than commuting recovery, which diverts demand away from retail and keeps RETAIL_REC lower over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose to 7.4 while WORKPLACES improved to -20.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS is positive while WORKPLACES is still materially negative and RETAIL_REC nonetheless rises in the next week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained narrowing of the gap between TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals coordinated mobility normalization, and this lagged recovery should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks once both series stop worsening.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves by at least 10 points while TRANSIT improves by at least 5 points from the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -53.9 to -43.6 and WORKPLACES improved from -51.7 to -20.6
failure_condition: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES meet the improvement trigger but RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days, the hypothesis is falsified.
